findings.status: resolved in subsequent coordinator fix; verified with 15 focused callback cases
findings.shot: fresh/input.js:24-26; Node fake-DOM multi-touch callback reproduction
findings.problem: With a guard pointer still down, pressing then releasing the separate lock button changes sampled guard from true to false. Unrelated action pointer cancellation or lost capture also clears guard.
findings.why: Touch-only players unexpectedly drop defense during simultaneous controls and cannot resume it without lifting and pressing the guard finger again.
findings.hypothesis: Confirmed by executing createInput: every touch button release callback deletes the same touchGuard entry, without checking the action or owning pointer.
findings.fix: Track guard ownership and restrict its release to guard pointers. Add node --test fresh/input.test.mjs cases for unrelated lock/attack/dodge pointerup, pointercancel and lostpointercapture while guard is held: all 9 must retain guard=true, and actual guard release, blur and setActive(false) must each yield false.

refutation.reason: Independent fake-DOM tests of actual createInput reproduced guard true-to-false for lock, attack and dodge releases. Keyboard Q masks but does not refute touch-only failure. Lock does not intentionally interrupt guard.

findings.status: resolved in subsequent coordinator fix; current HUD expression verified in 2 cases
findings.problem: The selected target is sentinel with 34 HP, but when retainer is closer the confrontation HUD displays retainer's 100 HP. The lock remains on sentinel.
findings.why: The visible selected opponent and its displayed health disagree, giving incorrect feedback during multi-enemy combat.
findings.hypothesis: Confirmed by source and expression execution: the HUD uses the nearest living enemy and treats world.locked only as a truthy gate instead of resolving that ID.
findings.fix: Resolve displayed health from the live enemy whose id equals world.locked. Add a test of the actual HUD implementation, run by node --test fresh/main.test.mjs, with locked sentinel=34 HP and nearer retainer=100 HP: displayed value must be 34; unlocked state must display no opponent health.
findings.evidence: evidence.observedReproductions[1]; simulation retains locked id until death or explicit unlock; presentation places selection ring on locked id.

refutation.reason: Independent code review confirmed no invariant keeps the locked enemy nearest. Movement changes nearest target while lock persists; ring ownership is correct and therefore does not reconcile incorrect HUD health.
